walkthroughs.body_html:
Philosophy of Religion: Self, Death & Afterlife — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Philosophy of Religion: Self, Death & Afterlife brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Philosophy of Religion: Self, Death & Afterlife.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What did Descartes claim about mind and body?
options: They are two distinct substances: a non-physical mind and a physical body
They are identical
Both are illusions
The body controls a purely chemical mind

mcqs.q: What does Hick's replica theory defend?
options: The logical possibility that God re-creates an exact replica of the dead person in another space
The claim that souls sleep until judgement day
The view that clones share one soul
The idea that memory alone is the soul

mcqs.q: What does the Buddhist teaching of anatta claim?
options: There is no permanent, unchanging self
The soul migrates unchanged between bodies
Only monks possess souls
The self is identical with Brahman

mcqs.q: What does a materialist typically conclude about death?
options: Consciousness depends on the brain, so it ceases when the brain dies
The soul escapes the body at death
Death is an illusion of the senses
Everyone is reincarnated according to karma

mcqs.q: Is resurrection the same as resuscitation of a corpse?
options: Dualism was proven in laboratory experiments in the 1960s.
Resurrection just means a dead body coming back to its old life.
No - in Christian teaching resurrection is transformation into glorified embodied life, as in Paul's 'spiritual body', not a mere return to ordinary mortal existence.
Resurrection means the soul becoming a ghost that haunts the earth.

mcqs.q: Does Buddhism teach that a soul transmigrates from body to body?
options: Buddhism and Hinduism teach exactly the same view of an immortal soul moving between bodies.
Resurrection means the soul becoming a ghost that haunts the earth.
Buddhism teaches that people are reborn only as animals.
No - rebirth occurs without a permanent soul; continuity is likened to one flame lighting another, which distinguishes Buddhist rebirth from Hindu reincarnation of the atman.

mcqs.q: Does being able to imagine leaving your body prove dualism?
options: Because I can imagine existing without my body, the soul must exist.
Buddhism teaches that people are reborn only as animals.
No - critics reply that conceivability does not establish real possibility, and materialists point to the close dependence of mind on brain as counter-evidence.
Dualism was proven in laboratory experiments in the 1960s.

free_texts.q: Name the Greek philosopher of the Theory of Forms.
free_texts.hint: Student of Socrates, teacher of Aristotle.

sequence.def: Phaedo, c.380 BC: immortal soul escapes the body
De Anima, c.350 BC: soul and body inseparable
Meditations, 1641: mind and body distinct substances
The Concept of Mind, 1949: dualism a category error
1976: God recreates the person after death
